document_check.note: Li B, Zeng B, Zeng P, Luo D, Yin F, Dong X, Peng Y, Xiang Y, Nie L, Li Y. Hippocampal-subfield macro- and microstructural changes in cerebral small vessel disease with mild cognitive impairment. J Affect Disord 2025;384:12-22. 58 CSVD-MCI, 54 CSVD-NCI and 57 controls; NODDI and FreeSurfer subfield volumes. Matches the review's Li et al. 2025a.

cited_result: Cross-sectional comparison of 58 CSVD-MCI with 54 CSVD-NCI patients (plus 57 controls). According to the Discussion, hippocampal volume did not differ between CSVD-MCI and CSVD-NCI, whereas NODDI FISO and NDI in left CA1-3 did. The principal result appraised is the CSVD-MCI vs CSVD-NCI difference in hippocampal-subfield FISO in the absence of a volume difference.
tool_reason: The cited result compares an imaging biomarker between diagnostic groups measured at one time point, and no discrimination accuracy is reported. The authors call the design cross-sectional, so the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist applies. Item mapping: exposure = cognitive group membership; condition = CSVD; outcome = hippocampal-subfield NODDI metrics and volumes.

domains.rationale: Age, handedness, CSVD imaging criteria, group-specific cognitive criteria and exclusions are all stated.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: The inclusion criteria for CSVD patients were: (1) age between 50 and 80 years; (2) right-handed; (3) meeting established CSVD criteria (Duering et al., 2023)

domains.rationale: Patients come from one hospital radiology service over a stated period, with demographics and risk factors in Table 1. The source of healthy controls is not described.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: We collected patients who underwent brain MRI examinations between October 2023 and May 2024 due to subjective memory decline or physical examination and were diagnosed with cerebral small vessel disease.

signalling.question: Is the recruitment source of the healthy controls described?
signalling.quote: Searched the Subjects section for where or how the 57 healthy controls were recruited. Only their eligibility criteria are given.

domains.domain: 3. Exposure (cognitive group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: The MCI classification rules are standard and explicit, but the reported MMSE values cannot be reconciled with them. A CSVD-MCI mean of 27.86 is impossible if every member had MMSE 24-26, and the CSVD-NC and control SDs are too large for a floor of 27. Whether the groups were formed as described therefore cannot be verified.

signalling.question: Was group membership (CSVD-MCI vs CSVD-NCI) determined validly and reliably?
signalling.quote: Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) score of 0.5, Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score ≤13 for illiterate group, ≤19 for primary school group, ≤24 for middle school and above group (Zhang et al., 2021), MMSE score between 24 and 26 (Jia et al., 2021)

signalling.question: Are the reported group characteristics consistent with the classification rules?

domains.domain: 4. Objective, standard criteria for the condition
domains.rationale: CSVD was defined by the published Duering et al. 2023 criteria with explicit Fazekas thresholds, and MCI by the Winblad et al. 2004 framework.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: meeting established CSVD criteria (Duering et al., 2023), ... deep white matter hyperintensity (WMH) Fazekas score ≥2, or periventricular WMH Fazekas = 3.

domains.rationale: Age, education, sex, vascular risk factors and WMH grade were compared between groups. WMH severity was identified as differing between CSVD-MCI and CSVD-NCI.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: t-test indicated differences in white matter hyperintensity between the CSVD-MCI and NCI groups. The three groups showed no significant differences in education level and age.

domains.rationale: ANCOVA adjusted only for age and education, which were balanced. WMH severity, the one identified factor that differed between the two CSVD groups (moderate-to-severe 77.6% vs 53.7%, p = 0.027), was not adjusted for or stratified. CSVD burden could plausibly raise both hippocampal free water and the probability of MCI, so the cited MCI vs NCI contrast is not protected from confounding.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated and adequate for the identified confounders?
signalling.quote: Between-group comparisons of hippocampal subfield volumes and NODDI metrics were conducted using analysis of covariance (ANCOVA), adjusting for age and years of education

signalling.question: Did the unadjusted factor differ between the compared groups?

domains.domain: 7. Outcomes (hippocampal NODDI and volume) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: The pipelines are standard (FreeSurfer 7.1, AMICO NODDI), and inter-rater agreement above 0.8 is stated, although the actual ICC values are not given. The authors acknowledge CSF partial-volume contamination of FISO at 2 mm resolution, which bears directly on the cited FISO-versus-volume contrast. Blinding of the raters to group is not reported.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
signalling.quote: Two senior radiologists visually assessed image segmentation and registration, with k > 0.8.

signalling.question: Is the principal outcome free of a known measurement artefact?
signalling.quote: larger voxels inevitably contain some CSF signals, which may contaminate the measurement of microstructural parameters, especially affecting the FISO index.

signalling.question: Were image raters blind to group membership?
signalling.quote: Searched for blind, masked or unaware in the image-processing and registration sections. None is reported.

domains.rationale: The analysis used covariate-adjusted ANCOVA (rank-based when non-normal), Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction and Tukey post hoc tests. The pairwise MCI vs NCI contrasts behind the cited result are reported only in supplementary tables not included in the document. The left CA1-3 NDI difference did not survive FDR (PFDR = 0.066).

signalling.question: Was appropriate statistical analysis used?
signalling.quote: Multiple comparisons were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure to control the false discovery rate (FDR), with a significance threshold set at adjusted P < 0.05; post hoc multiple comparisons were performed using Tukey's test.

overall: High (JBI analytical cross-sectional under this review's rule: 'strategies to deal with confounding' (item 6) is No).
overall_rationale: The one confounder that actually differed between the two CSVD groups compared in the cited result (WMH severity) was not adjusted for. In addition, the cognitive grouping cannot be verified against the reported MMSE values, and the FISO measure is exposed to acknowledged CSF partial-volume contamination. An item 6 of No makes the rating high under the review rule.

applicability.rationale: The sample is single-centre Chinese hospital patients aged 50-80 with moderate-to-severe WMH or lacunes. Stroke was excluded, and microbleeds and enlarged perivascular spaces were not characterised. Findings may not transfer to other CSVD or MCI populations.
